transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

I'm here because I've been dealing with constant, uncontrollable worry and extreme fatigue that leaves me completely exhausted. This has been going on for nearly two years now—about a year and ten months—and I just don't know what to do anymore.
During this time, have you been feeling down or depressed most days, or is the main problem the constant worry? Have there been stretches of two months or more when these symptoms went away?

The main issue is definitely the constant, uncontrollable worry rather than feeling depressed. It has been going on continuously for the last year and ten months, and I haven't had any breaks or stretches of two months where the symptoms went away.

Along with the worry, have you often had symptoms like feeling restless or on edge, muscle tension, trouble concentrating, irritability, or sleep problems? How many of those have been present most days?

I definitely experience severe, constant muscle tension in my neck, shoulders, and jaw, along with trouble concentrating because my mind fatigues quickly and worries constantly intrude. These physical and mental fatigue symptoms are present almost every day. However, I don't really experience restlessness, irritability, or sleep problems.
Has this worry and fatigue been causing significant problems in your work, school, relationships, or daily responsibilities?

Yes, it has been causing major problems because my loss of energy makes it extremely difficult to handle my daily responsibilities, and the mental fatigue makes it hard to concentrate. On top of that, these intrusive worries constantly spread to my work and family, which completely ruins my ability to focus and get things done.
Have these symptoms started or gotten worse with any medical illness, medications, caffeine or other substances, or have they happened only on their own?

I'm not really sure, but the symptoms seem to have happened completely on their own. I haven't noticed them being triggered or made worse by any medical illnesses, medications, caffeine, or other substances.
Do your worries involve many different areas of life, like work, family, finances, or health, rather than mainly one specific fear or sudden panic attacks?

Yes, my worries are definitely spread across many different areas like my work, family, and our finances rather than just one specific thing. I don't experience sudden panic attacks; it is more of a constant, generalized anxiety about almost every aspect of my daily life.
For at least six months, has this excessive worry been present more days than not and been hard to control?

Yes, absolutely. I've been dealing with this constant worry almost every single day for about a year and ten months now. Once a worry starts, it's incredibly difficult to control or stop, no matter how hard I try to distract myself.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports excessive, difficult-to-control worry across multiple life domains occurring nearly every day for about 1 year and 10 months, with associated muscle tension, concentration difficulty, and fatigue, causing significant functional impairment. There is no evidence here that the symptoms are better explained by substances, a medical condition, panic attacks, or a single circumscribed fear.
